answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use stake-weighted reputation with a slow thaw: each identity locks a refundable bond behind one public work history, like a single jetty reaching into shared waters. New identities start on a thin dune of trust with tiny quotas, and only verified, peer-attested work builds standing, like a juniper growing one branch per epoch. Clones must each pay the full bond, wait the full thaw, and redo the work, so farming a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds while an honest agent pays once.
